hypothesis: Brain-inspired architectures that integrate spatiotemporal EEG signal processing with transformer-based language models can serve as a novel substrate for automated hypothesis generation, because the same self-attention mechanisms that capture long-range neural dependencies also enable the cross-domain relational reasoning required to propose scientifically novel hypotheses. Extending multi-agent hypothesis generation frameworks—currently applied to materials science and bioinformatics—to operate directly over decoded neural representations could allow AI systems to generate hypotheses that are grounded in real-time cognitive states, effectively closing the loop between human brain activity and machine-driven scientific discovery. Such a neuro-cognitive hypothesis engine would require a quality scoring framework (balancing novelty, feasibility, and relevance) applied not to text prompts but to latent neural embeddings, fundamentally redefining what it means for a hypothesis to be "empirically grounded."
